curated.notes: Hand-curated local cost inputs for Groundwork. Every number has a source in its 'sources' list. null = not found from a citable source. Liquor fees: TX MB is a two-year fee; Chicago and Illinois license terms flagged in notes. workers_comp_per_100 is a national restaurant average (estimate) applied to every state; workers_comp_state_cost_index is a relative index (1.00 = median state), not a price.

CO.notes: SUI 3.05% all-in (1.53% base + 0.17% support + 1.35% bond surcharge per Eddy); DOL lists 1.53% base. Denver higher min wage.

$15.16 minus $3.02 tip credit = $12.14.
3.05% = 1.53% base + 0.17% support + 1.35% solvency surcharge. Payroll-vendor table; confirm with CDLE.
EY 2026 SUI wage bases: CO $30,600.
ESTIMATE. National restaurant average $1.06 per $100 payroll (2025); not Colorado-specific. NCCI states classify full-service as 9082 (not 9079). CO DOI approved -6.9% avg loss cost change for 2026.
Modeled relative index 0.83 (17% below median state). Not a price.

State form DR 8404 (via search snippet; PDF blocked automated fetch): $500 state H&R license fee + $1,100 new-application fee = $1,600 first year. Note C.R.S. 44-3-501 lists $75; the form figure is used as the current amount.
Statewide local license fee for H&R is $75 (B&W $48.75). Cities also charge a local application fee (Lone Tree: $1,000 new). Denver's own application fee was not found from an official source.

sources.note: Industrial Commission of Arizona: $15.15 from 2026-01-01; tipped $12.15 ($3 max tip credit).
2.00% new employer rate. Confirm with AZ DES.
ESTIMATE. National $1.06/$100; AZ is NCCI, full-service class 9082.
Relative index 0.86. Not a price.
A.R.S. 4-209: Series 12 $100 application + $1,500 issuance = $1,600; annual renewal $585. Third-party sites quote $2,100, which does not match statute.

City of Phoenix: $1,625 nonrefundable original-license application fee (City Clerk overview cites $1,455-$1,625), plus Series 12 city license fee $360 payable quarterly ($1,440/yr) per City Clerk fee schedule.
Series 6 (bar) and Series 7 are quota and trade on a secondary market; Series 12 restaurant is non-quota and non-transferable, so a restaurant usually does NOT need the secondary market.
Average Series 6 price in Maricopa County $94,650 quoted from DLLC staff. Aggregator ranges for metro Phoenix $80k-$150k (liquorlicensecost.com, 2026). Low confidence on recency.

No cheaper restaurant beer/wine-only license; Series 12 itself is $1,600. Series 7 state fees $100 + $1,500 + $175/yr renewal but it's a quota bar license (secondary price $34k-$55k per liquorlicensecost.com Goodyear page).

liquor.full_license_name: Series 12 Restaurant license (non-quota; requires 40%+ of gross from food)
liquor.beer_wine_name: Series 12 covers beer/wine/spirits; Series 7 Beer & Wine Bar is quota/transferable

Restaurant LBD fee by seats: $650 (40-74), $750 (75-125, used here), up to $1,200 (276+); plus $300 application fee = $1,050.

AK.notes: Min wage rose $13->$14 on 2026-07-01. No tip credit. SUI rate is Accommodation & Food Services (NAICS 72) employer rate; employees also pay 0.5%.

AL.notes: No state minimum wage law; federal applies.

AR.notes: Min wage for employers with 4+ employees. SUI: Eddy/Teamed 2.0% (incl. stabilization tax); DOL lists 1.8% base.

CA.notes: No tip credit. Some cities higher.

CT.notes: Tipped cash wage $6.38 for hotel/restaurant servers ($8.23 bartenders). DOL page lists tip credits ($10.56/$8.71), not cash wage.

DC.notes: Min wage $17.95->$18.40 and tipped $10.00->$10.30 on 2026-07-01 (amended Initiative 82).

FL.notes: Min wage rose $14->$15 and tipped $10.98->$11.98 on 2026-09-30; DOL page (2026-07-01) still shows $14.

GA.notes: State min $5.15 below federal; 7.25 used. SUI 2.7% all-in (DOL lists 2.64% + 0.06% admin assessment).

HI.notes: Tip credit $1.25 only if combined pay >= $7 above minimum.

IA.notes: Wage base cut from 2025 level by law.

LA.notes: No state min wage law. SUI new-employer rate = industry average (DOL 'IndAvg'; ~1-6.2% band); restaurant rate not found.

ME.notes: SUI: Eddy/Teamed 2.54% (likely incl. CSSF/UPAF); DOL lists 2.23% base (sources disagree).

MI.notes: Min wage rises to $15.00 on 2027-01-01; tipped rises toward 50% by 2031.

MN.notes: No tip credit. SUI new-employer rate set by industry (1-4.06% non-construction) + 0.4% base tax + 14% assessment; 2026 food-service rate not found (2022 table had 1.00%). Minneapolis/St Paul higher.

MT.notes: No tip credit (rate for businesses >$110k sales). SUI = Services industry 1.10% + 0.18% admin fund tax.

NE.notes: Min wage for 4+ employees. Wage base $24,000 for high-tax-group employers.

NH.notes: SUI 2.7% less 1.0% trust-fund-balance reduction (DOL lists 2.7% base); reduction confirmed Q1-Q2 2026.

NJ.notes: $15.23 for employers <6 employees/seasonal. Employees also contribute to UI.

NM.notes: SUI new-employer rate = industry average (~1.0-1.28%); restaurant rate not found. Eddy lists wage base $30,600 (outdated; DOL/NM DWS say $34,800).

NY.notes: Rest-of-state rates shown; NYC/Long Island/Westchester $17.00 min, $11.35 food-service cash wage. SUI 4.025% + 0.075% Re-employment Service Fund.

OH.notes: Min wage for gross receipts >= $405k. SUI 2.85% all-in per Eddy/Teamed; DOL lists 2.7% base.

OR.notes: Standard rate since 2026-07-01; Portland metro $16.80, nonurban $14.55. No tip credit.

PA.notes: Employees also pay UI on all wages.

RI.notes: SUI 1.0% + 0.21% job development assessment (DOL lists 1.0%). Wage base $32,300 for highest-rate employers.

SC.notes: No state min wage law. SUI 1.0% + 0.06% contingency assessment.

UT.notes: SUI new-employer rate = industry average benefit ratio (DOL 'IndAvg'); third-party 1.2% or 1.1% not verifiable.

WA.notes: No tip credit. SUI new-employer rate = 115% of industry average (min 1%); 2026 food-service rate not found. Seattle and others higher.

WI.notes: SUI 3.05% for taxable payroll < $500k (3.25% if >= $500k); DOL Jan-2026 table lists 2.5%.

WV.notes: Min wage for employers with 6+ employees at one location.

WY.notes: State min $5.15 below federal; 7.25 used. SUI new-employer rate by industry (DOL 'IndAvg'); sources conflict (1.69% vs 2.28-9.78%), restaurant rate not found.
